"I wish there was a one-size-fits-all solution to peeling this second skin off, but it is something that can only come with time, and reaffirming your worth. You shouldn't have to hold your breath waiting for that acceptance or love or recognition; it is right within you."

"I told my friends...the reasons I people please are the same reasons I look both ways when I cross the road  I don't wanna get hurt again. But we shouldn't spend our lives caging ourselves because of the fear of pain that is only inevitable and always temporary. Free yourself."

"I didn't learn or apply any pressure on myself to invest time, energy, and resources on myself because my whole identity was wrapped up in what I could give externally. I cannot tell you enough how that destroyed me. Don't make my same mistakes."

"And I think the self help community knows enough about the negative impacts of people pleasing already, but just to reiterate from my own personal experience  my chronic people pleasing has made me to abandon my adult needs and desires for nearly a decade."

"with depression there is a substantial lack of feeling safe in our own minds and emotional bodies. So of course we would seek out that security externally. And because of low self esteem, we'd often think we are not worthy or not enough for a good relationship already."

"I procrastinated on many things that would inch me closer to better self love. I had no other reason for ignoring or evading these things other than  I genuinely thought I was more useful being continuously available to drop everything, 24/7."
"I relish in the possibility that there is a distinct connection between living with depression and exhibiting Chronic People Pleasing behaviors. But the gist of it that I will leave here is that "

"To not have this left a deep, aching, gnawing void and in it's wake we clung to anything that was left  the affirmation that at one point when we did X Y or Z, we became someone who was sorely needed."

"This is about the people pleasing that persists when the threat has long passed. When the fear of it returning lingered so long that you resorted to these behaviors  this persona  so consistently that it became a second skin."
"It became our sense of safety  identity even  when the subject of our desire (to be accepted by this individual, to be loved, seen, heard) was no longer an active recipient of our projections."

"It became such an integral piece of you that often times, you just couldn't shut off. It was like a reflex, but more deeply embedded. To many of us, it replaced our mothers, our fathers, our ex lovers."
"Sometimes there are situations where you have to people please (or fawn) in order to survive or stay safe. But that's not quite what I'm talking about."
"Let's just call it what it is. Chronic People Pleasing is self harm. 🧵"
